verdict: Your B2B SaaS customer success work gives me a clear reason to keep reading. The portfolio and renewal work back up the Customer Success Manager title, and I’d move this forward with a question: what changed after you introduced the renewal-risk reviews?
write_up: Your resume points to customer success through the Northwind Analytics role, with earlier client account work at Brightpath Logistics. I read it for Customer Success Manager roles. The portfolio has a clear dollar value, but the resume says less about what happened with renewals, which matters for this kind of job.

The strongest line names the 32 B2B SaaS accounts and $2.4M in annual recurring revenue you managed. A recruiter can understand the portfolio without guessing. Your objective, on the other hand, could introduce almost any job and doesn't bring that work forward.

Let's start with the objective and the first Northwind line. Put customer success up top, then add what you handled in renewals and what the risk reviews uncovered. Keep the portfolio line as the model for making the work concrete.

cards.line: Results-driven, detail-oriented professional seeking a challenging role where I can utilize my skills.
cards.cannot_tell: This doesn't say which job you want or what you bring to it. Your customer success work is a much stronger introduction.
cards.example: Customer Success Manager | Managed 32 B2B SaaS accounts with $2.4M in annual recurring revenue
cards.question: Is Customer Success Manager the role you're targeting next?

cards.line: Responsible for managing customer relationships and renewals
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see the portfolio in the next line, but not what you handled in the renewal process or how renewals went.
cards.example: Managed customer relationships and renewals for 32 B2B SaaS accounts by [renewal work you handled], with [renewal result]
cards.question: What did you handle during renewals, and what renewal results can you share?

cards.line: Introduced monthly renewal-risk reviews across the portfolio
cards.cannot_tell: The monthly reviews are a useful detail. What they uncovered, and whether anything changed after them, isn't on the resume.
cards.example: Introduced monthly renewal-risk reviews across the portfolio to identify [renewal risks identified]
cards.question: What risks did the reviews identify?

cards.line: Team player with excellent communication skills
cards.cannot_tell: This asks a recruiter to take the skills on faith. Your business reviews give you a chance to show what you communicated instead.
cards.example: Ran quarterly business reviews with customer leadership teams covering [topics discussed]
cards.question: What did you discuss with customer leadership teams in those reviews?

cards.line: Assisted account managers with various tasks as needed
cards.cannot_tell: Assisted keeps your part appropriately modest, but various tasks doesn't say what the account managers relied on you to do.
cards.example: Assisted account managers with [tasks] for [client accounts or projects]
cards.question: Which tasks did you handle for the account managers, and for which accounts or projects?

cards.cannot_tell: Communication and leadership don't show how you used them. The list also doesn't name any tools you used for customer success work.
cards.question: Which customer success tools have you used, if any?

cards.line: Managed 32 B2B SaaS accounts with $2.4M in annual recurring revenue
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model: it names the accounts you managed and the recurring revenue attached to them. There's no guessing about how much business was in your portfolio.

fit.why: Your current role centers on B2B SaaS accounts, renewals and customer business reviews.
fit.level: mid-level, manages a B2B SaaS customer portfolio
fit.note: Your account coordination work supports the move into customer success. The Northwind role is the best place to show what you did with that portfolio.
